# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness more quickly than other kids her age, even after short periods of play, which may be related to a heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, including an aversion to certain foods, making mealtime stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and experiences seizures, which can be scary and require management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing concerns, as she doesn't always respond when called, which may indicate a hearing problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, where her eyes turn inward sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring careful brushing and a restricted diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delays and is not talking as much as other children her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a delayed fontanelle closure issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curved 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent chips or breaks
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing concerns
* Eyesight review to assess and manage vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to investigate potential heart conditions
* Referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and manage symptoms
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Management and treatment of epilepsy and seizures
* Support and management of feeding difficulties and dietary restrictions

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is a big issue, and has tried different diets and strategies to help him go more regularly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other children, and it's scary to watch, indicating potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had fluid in his ear, and has had to go to the doctor for that a few times, which has been a real challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs his eyes a lot when he's trying to focus on things, like he's straining or something, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble with harder foods, like apples or meat, and has to get creative with softer options or cutting things up into smaller pieces.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes longer to reach milestones than expected, which is hard to see, and the parents wish they could help him catch up faster.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school, and may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's developmental delay and potential behavioral issues are concerning, as he takes longer to reach milestones than expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental delay and behavioral differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of referral for specialist review, such as a pediatrician or a geneticist, to monitor for potential health concerns and provide supportive care.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a small hole in her heart that didn't close properly at birth, which requires regular monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be picky about food and refuses to eat certain things, which can be challenging at mealtimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may experience feeding difficulties, including lack of interest in feeding, which can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has low muscle tone, which affects her movement and play.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome may experience developmental delay, seizures, and other neurological issues, with around 20-40% of individuals reported to have seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the TV volume up high because she has difficulty hearing, and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is near-sighted and has trouble seeing things that are far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are prone to cavities due to weak enamel, and she needs to brush them regularly and visit the dentist often.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter-than-average fingers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of the spinal bones, short fingers, or curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and prevent dental issues
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor hearing loss and address any concerns
* Eyesight review to monitor vision problems and address any concerns

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences reluctance to eat, discomfort after eating, and difficulty chewing harder foods, indicating possible gastrointestinal issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord, which poses risks for spinal development and potentially overall neurological function.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues such as developmental delay.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty hearing in noisy environments and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on objects or toys, suggesting a potential issue with vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and may have weak enamel, requiring regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, requiring regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient may require extra help in school and potentially need special schooling or an Educational Health Care Plan.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or an Educational Health Care Plan.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delay and may require targeted therapies to support overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord, which poses risks for spinal development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some may have short fingers or other skeletal anomalies.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health and address any concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight review to monitor vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health.
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor skeletal development.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support overall development.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
